name: DPRK-Style Revenue Generation: Cyber Theft and Overseas IT Workers (Indicator Level)
description: State-linked actors may raise revenue through cyber-enabled theft of virtual assets and funds, and through overseas IT workers who conceal identity and location. This typology is described only at indicator level to support detection and screening, without operational detail.

sources.text: FATF, Guidance on Counter Proliferation Financing (2018)
FATF, Targeted Update on Implementation of the FATF Standards on Virtual Assets and VASPs (annual, 2019 onward)
US State/Treasury/FBI, Guidance on the Democratic People's Republic of Korea Information Technology Workers (May 2022); US Government, Guidance on the North Korean Cyber Threat (April 2020)

indicators.name: Freelancer or contractor accounts with identity and location inconsistencies
indicators.canon: Inconsistent or synthetic identity data at onboarding
indicators.desc: Identity documents, contact details, geolocation or device data do not align, suggesting fabricated, stolen or misrepresented identity.
indicators.ctx: Remote worker profile shows mismatched documents, geolocation and payment details.
indicators.fp: Remote workers legitimately use VPNs and travel.

indicators.name: Payments to accounts held by third parties on behalf of workers
indicators.canon: Workers paid to third-party or multiple accounts
indicators.desc: Wages are paid to accounts not held by the worker or split across several accounts.
indicators.ctx: Earnings are routed to accounts of unrelated people or to multiple wallets, then consolidated.
indicators.fp: Agencies and family members sometimes receive payments.

indicators.name: Inflows of stolen virtual assets traced by analytics
indicators.canon: Exposure to wallets attributed to designated, stolen-fund or illicit actors
indicators.desc: Customer transacts directly or near-directly with blockchain addresses attributed by sanctions lists or analytics to designated persons, thefts, ransomware or terrorist fundraising.
indicators.ctx: Deposits with direct or near-direct exposure to addresses attributed to major thefts.
indicators.fp: Exposure may be indirect and unknowing.

indicators.name: Rapid chain-hopping and conversion following inbound funds
indicators.canon: Chain-hopping through bridges shortly after receipt
indicators.desc: Virtual assets are moved across chains or bridges and converted soon after being received.
indicators.ctx: Assets are swapped across chains and tokens in quick succession before off-ramp.

indicators.name: Off-ramp via over-the-counter brokers in higher-risk jurisdictions
indicators.canon: Use of OTC desks or brokers with minimal due diligence for conversion to fiat
indicators.desc: Large over-the-counter trades or fiat off-ramps via brokers that avoid identity verification, pay via third parties or operate outside strong supervision.
indicators.ctx: Large conversions to fiat at OTC desks outside strong supervision.

indicators.name: Entities and individuals linked to sanctioned networks
indicators.canon: Ownership or controllers linked to designated or previously reported parties
indicators.desc: Owners, officers or associates match sanctions or designation lists, prior suspicious reports or adverse media.
indicators.ctx: Customer matches or is linked to designated persons or front entities in public lists.

indicators.name: Bank accounts opened for IT-services companies with minimal footprint
indicators.desc: Business shows little or no staff, premises, web presence or client base consistent with its stated activities and turnover.
indicators.ctx: Foreign IT-services firm has limited verifiable clients and unclear service delivery.

indicators.name: Use of multiple identities or fabricated credentials in onboarding
indicators.canon: Use of multiple identities or fabricated credentials in onboarding
indicators.desc: Documents, employment history or references show signs of fabrication.
indicators.ctx: Documents, employment history or references show signs of fabrication.
